title: Hiring-threshold price gate scan
body:
Purpose:
Quick scan to establish hiring thresholds (H) where price movements (P) force capacity reallocation or a pause on new hires. This is a lightweight working sheet for the exec review on 2026-02-08. Not final — focuses on short lead decisions (30–90d) rather than multi-year planning.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- If hosted per-token price drops <= 12% we can defer 8 FTEs from the mid-cycle hiring plan without impacting 99th percentile latency SLAs (assuming current batching and KV cache).
- If per-token price rises +18% (pessimistic shock), we need a hiring freeze and immediate reallocation of $1.6M budget to burst-reserve capacity to avoid SLA breaches for enterprise customers.
- The chart below maps price deltas to headcount delta and near-term EBITDA swing. Use as an operational triggerboard; thresholds are provisional.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline period: run-rate Oct–Dec 2025, average token mix: 60% short-chat, 30% long-completion, 10% embeddings.
- Baseline unit cost (hosted): $0.0009/token equivalent (weighted).
- Average loaded cost per new infra engineer hire (total comp + benefits + ramp): $220k/year.
- GPU spot pool + cloud egress margin currently ~ $18k/month for a 16-GPU pool sized for 100k qps-equivalent.
- Operational levers: batching tuning (~10–20% cost saving), prefix cache enabling (up to 15% token reduction), quantized model rollout (permanent -20% cost on heavy workloads but 1.5x eval QA overhead).

Scenario sheet (30–90d impact):
| Scenario name | Price delta | HC delta (FTE) | Near-term EBITDA delta (annualized) | Key ops action |
|---------------|-------------:|---------------:|------------------------------------:|----------------|
| Favorable glide | -12% | -8 | +$860k | Delay 4 backend hires + 4 infra hires, activate batch suggestion set A |
| Mild compression | -5% | -3 | +$210k | Slow contractor conversions, push quantization pilot to Q3 |
| Baseline | 0% | 0 | $0 | No change (monitor consumption) |
| Price uptick | +10% | +0 | -$420k | Activate cost-governor flags, restrict non-core product experiments |
| Shock | +18% | +0 (freeze) | -$1.6M | Hiring freeze + burst reserve purchase + customer SLA migration plan |

Notes on the table: FTE reductions imply hiring deferral, not layoffs. EBITDA deltas incorporate both salary spacing and immediate one-time infra purchase where noted. All numbers rounded.

Small-sheet snapshot (CSV view):

favorable,-0.12,-8,860000,"delay 4 pd + 4 infra, enable batch A"
mild,-0.05,-3,210000,"slow conversions, quant pilot Q3"
baseline,0,0,0,"monitor"
uptick,0.10,0,-420000,"enable cost-governor, limit experiments"
shock,0.18,0,-1600000,"hiring freeze, buy burst reserve, SLA migration"

Open questions / risks (to resolve before exec sign-off):
- How correlated is spot GPU pricing to token price movement? Current model assumes partial correlation but we need verification from infra procurement (PR-1298).
- What fraction of enterprise demand can be routed to Dedicated accounts without breaking contractual SLAs? Legal needs to review customer contracts for migration allowances.
- Quantization QA: cost and duration assumptions rely on a 6-week QA window; if that slips to 10 weeks, net benefit drops ~35%.

Workplan (next actions):
- Finance: run a Monte Carlo variant with token mix shift +/- 10% by 2026-03-01 (owner: Miguel).
- Infra: confirm spot pool elasticity curve (owner: Jonah) and validate the $18k/month baseline.
- Product: freeze non-core experiments if price > +10% for 14 days (owner: Aisha).
- Legal: quick-check migration clauses by 2026-02-12 (owner: Priya, tagged).

Decision heuristics (proposed triggerboard):
- If short-window price change > +12% for 7 consecutive days -> declare 'price shock' and enact hiring freeze + immediate procurement of burst reserve.
- If price change < -8% sustained for 21 days -> acceleration signal: convert 50% of contractor pipeline to FTE (capped at 6 hires).

Appendix: quick calcs (rounded):
- Savings from deferring 8 hires = 8 * $220k = $1.76M (annualized). We only count 50% in 12-month run to be conservative -> $880k, aligns to table ~ $860k after other offsets.
- Burst reserve cost to cover shock for 90 days = ~$400k (one-time) + operational margin = $480k -> impacts near-term cash but protects contract revenue.

TODOs and orange flags: 
- [ ] Re-run numbers against actual Dec-2025 token mix (data request: BI export DEC2025_TOKEN_MIX.csv).
- [ ] Confirm whether quantization rollout affects model latency by >5% (prod-qa test).
- [ ] Add per-region sensitivity (NA vs EU) — this doc currently uses blended view.

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep the decision heuristics short and automatable — attach to the finance runbook and make alerts in PagerDuty if thresholds hit.
- We should also map to sales credits; if price shock fires, pre-authorize up to $250k credits to keep top 10 accounts online while infra catches up.

Bottom line: operational triggers > +12% or <-8% should be the only things that auto-change hiring posture. Everything else passes through a 1-week review loop. This gives a manageable, measurable policy for the 30–90d horizon.

quick_decision: Provisional trigger: price > +12% for 7 days = hiring freeze + procure burst reserve; price < -8% for 21 days = accelerate contractor conversions (cap 6 hires).
